extracted.intended_audience: technology-interested readers and product teams concerned with AI in consumer news apps
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluative criteria for deploying or judging generative-AI features that produce news summaries/alerts in consumer apps, with emphasis on accuracy, attribution, bias mitigation and responsible rollout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of AI-generated summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: AI-generated summaries and notifications must be accurate; the feature has generated some inaccurate alerts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of failures include summaries falsely stating a suspect had shot himself and claiming sporting results before events concluded. Anti-pattern: releasing summaries that contradict original source content. Scoring note: high-quality implementations should minimize hallucinations and factual errors through testing and guardrails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear attribution when text is AI-generated
rubrics_metrics.description: Make clear when notifications or summaries are generated by Apple Intelligence (or another AI) rather than originating from the publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple plans a software update to 'further clarify' when displayed text is an AI summarisation. Guidance: explicit labelling/disclosure prevents user confusion; simply clarifying attribution without addressing accuracy is inadequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid impersonating reputable publishers
rubrics_metrics.description: AI outputs should not appear to come from trusted news organisations (e.g., BBC) when they are AI-generated summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem example: AI notifications looked like they were coming from the BBC, undermining trust. Implementations must ensure the visual/source cues make clear the distinction between original publisher content and AI-generated summaries to avoid misleading users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough testing before public rollout
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not push out AI-driven features before they are ready; perform extensive testing to catch inaccuracies and harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article describes both Apple and Fable as having 'pushed out AI driven features before they were ready.' Guidance: pre-release testing should include factuality checks, edge-case scenarios, and user trials; anti-pattern: rushing to market for commercial reasons without adequate QA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rapid, responsible response to user complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should respond promptly and substantively to complaints about AI outputs rather than being slow or silent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece criticises Apple's 'lack of response' and 'slowness of its response.' Good practice: investigate reports quickly, communicate findings, and deploy fixes; poor practice: ignoring or downplaying legitimate user concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset quality and bias mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure training data is not skewed toward offensive or unrepresentative perspectives; biased training data can produce bigoted outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fable's model produced bigoted, racist language because the training data contained biased content ('almost nothing but a “straight, cis white man’s perspective”'). Guidance: curate datasets, apply debiasing techniques, and audit outputs for harmful stereotypes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove or disable features that cause harm
rubrics_metrics.description: If an AI-driven feature causes harm in the community, it should be removed or disabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fable removed three AI-reliant features (including the wrapped summary) after reports of harmful summaries. Policy: prioritize user safety and community standards over keeping problematic features active.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not prioritise commercial launch over safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should not rush generative-AI functionality to market for commercial reasons at the expense of safety and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commentary calls this haste irresponsible and a cautionary tale. Guidance: align go-to-market decisions with robust risk assessment and mitigation rather than marketing deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify temporality and avoid premature claims
rubrics_metrics.description: AI summaries must respect timing and verification; they should not state outcomes or facts (e.g., match results) before events have occurred or been confirmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example failure: telling users a player had won a championship before the match began. Guidance: include checks on time-sensitive information and avoid definitive language when facts are pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about beta status and ongoing improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly indicate when AI features are in beta and communicate that improvements are ongoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apple noted 'Apple Intelligence features are in beta and we are continuously making improvements with the help of user feedback.' Guidance: transparency helps set user expectations, but should be paired with concrete safety/accuracy measures rather than used to excuse poor performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to responsible and ethical AI development
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrable commitment to ethical, responsible development of generative AI features is required, not just cosmetic fixes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Apple's response 'doesn’t exactly instill confidence' in its commitment to responsible development. Guidance: publish safety practices, invest in mitigation, and prioritize ethical standards throughout product lifecycle.
